Starting points

Start With One Problem.

A path is one paper problem, the form that fixes it, and the automation that comes next.

To consider

Three Possible Starting Points

Each one is the first step on a path, and each already has a client story on your site.

Onboarding paperwork

Forms and attachments are scattered, links don't work, and someone has to chase every signature.

  • Who it's for: HR and volunteer offices, mostly at school districts
  • Forms to start with: New employee onboarding, Volunteer applications
  • Then automation: Approvals that route on their own, with every form saved to the right record.
  • What you already have: Two client stories already on your site: HR Onboarding of New Employees, and Volunteer Onboarding at a School District.

Time cards and payroll

Paper time cards pile up, until hundreds of cards turn into thousands.

  • Who it's for: Payroll and site offices, mostly at school districts
  • Forms to start with: Time cards, Mileage forms
  • Then automation: Supervisor approval in order, then hours handed to payroll without retyping.
  • What you already have: One client story on your site: Paper Time Cards. A district time card project is also underway.

Purchasing and payments

Purchase orders are handled by hand, and payments slip through the cracks.

  • Who it's for: Finance and purchasing offices at counties, cities, and other public agencies
  • Forms to start with: Purchase orders, Invoices
  • Then automation: Approvals routed by department, with a clear record of who approved what.
  • What you already have: One client story on your site: Purchase Orders, Invoices, and Payments.

Sample

Onboarding Paperwork

Who to call

HR and volunteer offices, mostly at school districts

First question

When someone new is hired, how many forms do they fill out, and where do those forms go?

Demo with

New employee onboarding

Story to tell

Two client stories already on your site: HR Onboarding of New Employees, and Volunteer Onboarding at a School District.

The steps

From First Call to Next Path

01

Pick

Choose the customers on your list who have this problem. Start with people we already work with.

02

Open

Ask the first question. Listen before talking about OneForm.

03

Meet

Offer lunch with their team, or a visit to the booth.

04

Show

Demo the starting form, using their own paper form if they'll share it.

05

Start

Walk them through the onboarding roadmap and agree on a first step.

06

Stay

Keep sending the project updates, then suggest their next path.
